title: Transmission of Multiple Signals through an Optical Fiber Using Wavefront Shaping
protocol: Place and fix the laser to provide a collimated light beam.
Put the polarizing beam splitter (PBS) to split the laser beam into reference and object beams.
Rotate the half wave plates (HWP) until the power of the reference beam and object beam is roughly equal.
Check the balance by putting a screen in both the reference and object beams.
Choose the PBS orientation so that the polarization of the reference beam fits the spatial light modulator (SLM).
Put a beam splitter (BS) into the reference beam to split it into two beams.
Place optical modulators (OM) such that these two beams pass through OM1 and OM2, respectively.
Combine the two beams from OM1 and OM2 at BS2 using mirrors.
Adjust the beam splitters and mirrors so that both beams are spatially separated.
Carefully align BS5 to ensure perpendicular incidence of both beams on the SLM pixel plane.
Adjust the position and distance between two lenses in a Keplerian telescope to get a sharp image of the SLM plane on the CMOS camera.
Ensure that the flat sides of L1 and L2 face each other to minimize aberrations.
Use BS7 to split the object beam into two beams and combine them at BS8 using mirrors.
Adjust the beam splitters and mirrors so that both beams are spatially separated.
Deflect both beams using BS9 toward the microscope objective (OBJ).
Focus OBJ2 on the distal end of the multimode fiber (MMF) and check focus by observing back reflection from MMF with L3 and CCD camera.
Collimate light from the object beam exiting the MMF using OBJ1.
Split the object beam using BS6, ignoring linear polarizer at first.
Combine both object beams with reference beams at BS3 and BS4 using mirrors.
Adjust beam splitters and mirrors so that each pair of reference and object beam overlap at SLM, intersecting with a small angle (less than 1°).
Turn orientation of HWP to ensure power of the reference and object beam are approximately equal.
Check the interference pattern at the CMOS camera.
Adjust the intersection angle until the interference fringe spacing equals two pixels on the CMOS camera.
Match the orientation of the LP to the polarization of object and reference beams for maximum contrast in the CMOS camera image.
Illuminate the whole SLM using only one of the reference beams.
Block all other reference and object beams.
Capture an image of the SLM with the CMOS camera.
Get the coordinates of the upper left corner of the SLM in the CMOS camera image.
Use these pixel coordinates as the point of origin regarding the SLM.
Remove all beam blocks.
Block both reference beam 2 and object beam 2.
Capture an image of the hologram with the CMOS camera.
Evaluate the phase in the recorded hologram using angular spectrum method.
Calculate the inverted phase in the corresponding region of beam 1.
Block both reference beam 1 and object beam 1.
Capture an image of the hologram with the CMOS camera.
Measure the phase in the recorded hologram using angular spectrum method again.
Calculate the inverted phase at the corresponding region of beam 2.
Remove all beam blocks.
Block the object beam.
Stitch the calculated inverted phase images at the corresponding regions of beam 1 and 2 together.
Display the entire image on the SLM, typically using the computer graphics port.
Start the modulation of the input signals 1 and 2 by activating OM1 and OM2.
Observe the output signals 1 and 2 on the CCD camera.
